To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
mismatch repair (MMRH) activates c-Abl/p53 family member p73α/GADD 45α-mediated apoptosis, but not p53-mediated G2 arrest, to induce cell death.
MMR-dependent G1 arrest is p53-dependent, whereas MMR-dependent G 2 arrest and apoptosis are p53-independent and are mediated by c-Abl/p53α/GADD45a retrograde signaling.
MMR-dependent intrinsic cell death is p53-independent but stimulated by hmlh1/c-Abl-mediated retrograde signaling to activate p73α/GADD-45α.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of MMR in DNA damage responses, and the signaling pathways that regulate cell death.
the identification and characterization of the molecular pathways that control cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in cells with functional MMR.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie MMR-dependent G1/S checkpoint arrest and cell death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MMR-dependent GADD45α and p53-independent apoptosis is stimulated by hMLh1/c-Abl/73α signaling.
MMR-dependent intrinsic cell death is p53-independent and stimulated by hMLLH1/c-ABL/p73α/GDD45α retrograde signal transduction.
MMR-dependent activation of p53, c-Abl, and p73α are all involved in MMR-dependent GADD45α-mediated cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MMR-dependent activation of c-Abl, which in turn activates p73α and its downstream target, GADD45α, is required for MMR-dependent GADD45α-mediated intrinsic apoptosis.
MMR-dependent GADD45α up-regulation is mediated by hMLH-1 and c-Abl, which are upstream of p73α.
MMR-dependent G1/S arrest and G2 arrest are p53-dependent and p53-independent, respectively, and that MMR-dependent apoptosis is p53-dependent, but not p53-independent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MMR-dependent GADD45α activation is a key event in apoptosis, and uncoupling of G2 arrest from apoptosis may be an effective therapeutic strategy to prevent MMR-deficient tumor progression.
the DNA mismatch repair system can be used to activate the p73α/GADD 45α-mediated apoptosis pathway.
MMR-dependent intrinsic cell death is a p53-independent, c-Abl/p53α/GADD45a retrograde signaling pathway that is uncoupled from G2 arrest and lethality.
